articleTitle: Optimizing Traffic Light Control using YOLOv8 for Real-Time Vehicle Detection and Traffic Density
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The problem of traffic congestion becomes crucial as the number of vehicles on the roads, especially in big cities, continues to rise. An effective and cost-efficient solution is managing traffic lights based on density. This paper introduces a method utilizing deep neural networks to control traffic lights by analyzing surveillance camera footage and adjusting the lights automatically. Specifically, we employ the state-of-the-art YOLOv8 model to identify vehicles on the road from camera images, assess traffic density, and optimize the timing of traffic lights accordingly. The evaluation results show that the proposed model demonstrates a high accuracy in vehicle detection, achieving a mAP50 of up to $\mathbf{9 7 \%}$. In addition, the results of vehicle counting and traffic light control are also tested in various contexts.

articleTitle: Electronic Element Parameter Estimation of Amplifier Circuit using Regression Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper discusses the pivotal role of integrated circuits (ICs) in contemporary electronic devices and the component error issues they encounter. ICs facilitate the rapid advancement of electronic technology through a high degree of integration; however, the intricate fabrication process and delicate operations during manufacturing lead to component errors, which have become an urgent challenge in the testing domain. To address this, the paper proposes a novel test scheme based on S-parameters and regression algorithms. This approach measures S-parameters through computer-aided virtual simulation technology and a network analyzer, and combines various common regression algorithms to predict the parameters of the circuit components. A comparative analysis of these algorithms is conducted, laying the foundation for subsequent testing of circuit components.

articleTitle: An Efficient Hardware Implementation of Spiking Neural Network Using Approximate Izhikevich Neuron
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Implementation of a highly complicated spiking neuron model on the hardware often requires a large amount of hardware resources. To deal with this problem, the mathematical accuracy of the neuron model needs to be compromised to allow for a more efficient implementation. In this paper, we utilize Approximate Computing to achieve the trade-offs between computational accuracy and hardware requirements. Instead of naively applying approximate adders and approximate multipliers to the Izhikevich model, this work explores different combinations of adders and multipliers in conjunction with an approximate aware approach. The evaluation results of STDP-trained Spiking Neural Networks with 6,400 neurons show that with a proper approximation technique, the highest accuracy of the approximate neuron model is $81.9 \%$, which suffers a $1.5 \%$ accuracy loss but reduces area cost and power consumption of the neuron by $40.3 \%$ and $24.2 \%$ respectively when compared to the accurate version of the Izhikevich neuron model.

articleTitle: Low-latency Elliptic Curve Scalar Multiplication Accelerator on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Elliptic curve cryptography (ECC) is an important building block for providing us with digital security nowadays and likely also in the future. Being able to compute the elliptic curve scalar multiplication (ECSM) fast would make the realtime complex cryptosystem more practical to be used in our lives. To meet those needs, we propose minor optimizations to Lookup Table Modular Reduction (LUTMR) to further reduce the modular multiplication latency. Then, we propose the ECSM accelerator that builds on a 5-stage modular multiplier based on the LUTMR technique together with a tight schedule for computing the Add/Double Mongomery ladder. Our architecture works on any Weierstrass curve, is constant-time, and is protected from simple power analysis (SPA). We demonstrate its performance by implementing the accelerator on Virtex 7 (Virtex Ultrascale+) FPGA for five curves which are Secp256k1, NIST-P256, BN254, NIST-P381, and BLS12-381. The latency for computing ECSM are $53.3,52.6,53.2,88.1$, and $71.8 \mu \mathrm{s}(27.1,27.8,29.2,44.5$, and $40.8 \mu \mathrm{s})$ respectively. These are the lowest ever reported latency among the state-of-the-art architecture while also lowest in the normalized area-time criteria among the generic architecture.

articleTitle: Low-power Data Protection for Energy-harvesting Beat Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Beat sensors are novel power-harvested devices with ultra-low-power sensing mechanisms that can collect data and send it using LoRa using millijoules of energy. Instead of reading the sensor values using ADC, beat sensors are carefully designed to sense the data and encode the values in the interval times of data transmission. However, no security mechanisms have been integrated to protect the collected data because of the limited power supply. In this paper, we will analyze the security problems in beat sensors and propose lightweight data protection mechanisms while considering the power budget. The proposed data protection method has been implemented in software on an STM32 controller using True Random Number Generators and lightweight blockcipher Simon and Speck, and it has been tested in the Beat Sensor system.

articleTitle: VNEMOS: Vietnamese Speech Emotion Inference Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This research introduces the dataset that we created to test voice emotional recognition models with Vietnamese data. The data set is the result of research, testing, and filtering 250 emotional segments from movie, movie series and live show divided equally for 5 basic emotional states of humans: “anger, happiness, sadness, neutral and anxiety”, VNEMOS contains approximately 30 minutes long. This dataset brings a balanced and diverse emotional set to study emotional recognition issues related to understanding human mood and emotions. Through evaluation Our dataset achieved a $89 \%$ accuracy, showcasing the adeptness at capturing the essence of positive emotions and robust learning capabilities in real-world scenarios. By clarifying these nuances. Our research will contribute much to future work on emotion recognition and signal processing in Vietnamese and data using human psychological science. Detailed information of the dataset is in the following link: “bit.ly/VNEMOS”

articleTitle: A whisker sensor with a tetrapod particle-infused jamming actuator for extensive measurement range
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The whisker sensor, with its long and slender shape, bends in response to external forces, enabling it to measure force or strain. To enhance sensitivity, it is advantageous for whiskers to bend easily, for which soft polymers are used. Since the bending magnitude changes with the Young’s modulus of the soft polymer, the measurement range of the sensor is determined by the material composing the whisker, assuming the structure remains the same. Meanwhile, the jamming effect, previously utilized to adjust the stiffness of soft actuators/grippers, involves the change in stiffness through the alteration of the spatial occupancy rate of spherical particles within a soft chamber, as the internal pressure is adjusted. For the first time, we applied the jamming effect to the whisker sensors, developing a whisker sensor with a variable stiffness that allows for a wide measurement range. Notably, using tetrapod particles instead of spherical ones increased the sensor’s measurement range by 2.7 times, maintaining an average sensitivity of $80 \mathrm{~mm} / \mathrm{N}$ within the measurement range. Particularly, to enhance the jamming effect, tetrapod particles, which have a higher contact area and thus greater friction between particles compared to spherical ones, were used in the jamming actuators. Consequently, the whisker sensor demonstrated the capability to measure with high sensitivity across a range of $0-240 \mathrm{mN}$ by effectively utilizing both soft and stiff modes. Therefore, the reported whisker sensor is expected to contribute to the improvement of sensor performance in measuring fine forces.

articleTitle: Surgical Tool Detection and Pose Estimation using YOLOv8-pose Model: A Study on Clipper Tool
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Analyzing or understanding medical images obtained from an endoscopic camera is important in computerassisted interventions (CAI). Compared to prior research, this paper introduces a method for detecting surgical tools and simultaneously estimating their pose. We collected and labeled data for the clipper tool to train based on the YOLOv8-pose model. The model was assessed on a test dataset using 4 different versions of the YOLOv8-pose model. Among these versions, YOLOv8n, with just 3M parameters (the lightest variant), demonstrates notably high accuracy in pose estimation. It achieves Precision, Recall, respectively. Furthermore, this version shows impressive accuracy in clipper detection, with Precision, Recall, mAP50, and mAP5095 scores of $\mathbf{9 7. 9 \%}, \mathbf{9 6. 0 \%}, \mathbf{9 9. 2 \%}$, and $\mathbf{6 4. 6 \%}$, respectively. These impressive results can pave the way for further development of this approach for various types of surgical tools in the future.

articleTitle: Design and Integration of Digital Thermal Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, the design and integration of a digital thermal sensor (DTS) is presented inside a System On Chip (SOC). This work proposes a bandgapbased voltage reference with Analog-to-Digital-Converter (ADC) to realize a DTS with improved accuracy and fast temperature readouts. The DTS has a temperature readout accuracy of $+1.5 \mathrm{C}-3 \mathrm{C}$ across a wide range of temperatures. We present the analog integration challenges that SOCs having multiple supply domains face in integrating the DTS and the techniques used to overcome them. Furthermore, we showcase how we minimize the noise coupling and improve the speed on the sensitive routes used to read temperatures. We believe our work is valuable to the SOC design community and will help address the issue of steep thermal gradients present in the latest process nodes and also drive down the thermal cooling costs by using proactive measures.

articleTitle: A Ku-band SIW Power Divider With High Isolation Using Coupled Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for designing power dividers with high isolation using coupled substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonators. Building on a conventional structure, we introduce two improved types of power dividers. By strategically adjusting the placement of the ports, we enhance the overall performance of the divider. Both types of dividers can operate over a fractional bandwidth of $\mathbf{5. 3 \%}$ in the Ku-band, demonstrating good insertion loss and highly balanced amplitude and phase. The best design exhibits return losses greater than 13.8 dB, divided insertion losses greater than 4.6 dB, and isolation between output ports greater than 19.7 dB across the entire band.

articleTitle: Advancing Robust Few-shot Surface Defect Detection through Meta-learning
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The primary limitation of deep learning (DL) techniques in detecting manufacturing defects is the requirement for a substantial volume of labeled data. Nevertheless, obtaining precise annotations is an arduous process due to the diverse range of defect categories. To tackle this issue, we propose MetaFormer, a transformer-based few-shot surface defect detection that learns the meta-features from a large-scale dataset of base classes. This method enables generalization to a novel class with only a few training examples. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our model on the steel surface defect dataset, surpassing the performance of the baseline model despite using only a limited number of annotated examples.

articleTitle: Microwave and Millimeter Wave Rectennas with Gated Anode Diode and Diode on Antenna Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper presents rectenna topologies that are diode on antenna (DoA) for highly-efficient rectification and gated anode diode (GAD) for high-power one. First of all, DoA topology with a high-impedance dipole antenna including all of RF circuit functionalities is discussed for highly efficient rectification in 5.8 GHz band. The rectifier diodes are directly connected to the antennas without lossy circuit components. In the next discussion, for high-power operation in 5.8 GHz band, a gated anode diode (GAD) configured with gate-drain connected GaAs E-pHEMT is demonstrated for the rectifier instead of GaAs SBD. Finally, DoA topology with a wire-loop antenna is demonstrated for highly efficient rectification in 28 GHz band. In addition, the antenna configuration realizes high radiation gain with the wire and inductive impedance for DoA topology with the loop. It eliminates circuit loss which is more serious in the millimeter wave band.

articleTitle: Enhancing functional verification productivity through an automated workflow with Machine Learning based tools
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: As the demand for chips grows and high-performance processing requirements increase, chip designs have become larger and more complex. Consequently, the verification time for large-scale System on Chip (SoC) has dramatically increased. To keep up with this growth, there is a need to enhance the verification process and workflow, aiming to improve efficiency and productivity. In this paper, we propose a verification automation workflow driven by Machine Learning (ML)-based Electronic Design Automation (EDA) tools, which can enhance productivity in two key areas: regression testing and debugging of regression failures. By using this methodology, we can improve Turn-Around Time (TAT) by up to $40 \%$ while maintaining the same coverage for random test regression. Additionally, for debugging, the ML-based tool can help to automate the debugging process for regression failures, resulting in a workload reduction of up to $75 \%$ compared to the original workflow, specifically for four significant debugging issues: failure triage, bad revision detection, source code diff check and waveform difference identification.

articleTitle: Push and Pull Robot with Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The objective of this research is to study how basic reinforcement learning (RL) techniques can be applied to dynamic push and pull tasks for a mobile robot. Our goal is to determine the ideal combination of rewards and punishments to improve the learning process by utilizing fundamental concepts of reinforcement learning and closely monitoring the robot’s interactions with its dynamic environment. The research entails creating algorithms specifically designed to handle the special difficulties presented by push and pull jobs, and then rigorously testing and simulating these algorithms. We hope to identify trends and behaviors through this method that will aid in creating an effective and adaptable robotic system. As the research developed, it concentrated on creating algorithms and assessing pre-existing ideas, offering insightful information about the usefulness of reinforcement learning for mobile robots in dynamic environments. The study opens the door for further developments in this area by providing a thorough understanding of RL’s influence on adaptive robotic systems.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Low-Power VCO-based ADC for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The paper presents the design of an Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC) using Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO)based ADC techniques, calibrated for Internet of Things (IoT) applications with a power supply of only 1.3 V targeting Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). The flexible integration between analog and digital elements of the VCO-based ADC technology minimizes design time and energy consumption. The paper also focuses on maximizing the performance of VCO through the use of low-pass filtering, analog calibration to lower variability, oversampling to increase signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and the removal of unneeded samples to improve VCO’s output resolution. The free and open-source SkyWater 130nm PDKs and tools were employed for both design and simulation. The simulation results show that the proposed ADC achieves 8 -bit effective number of bits (ENOB), with a 50 dB SNR and a just 0.042 mW power consumption.

articleTitle: Development of low-cost myoelectric prosthetic hand with force feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Transradial amputations, also known as below-elbow amputations, can occur for various reasons, including trauma, congenital limb deficiencies, vascular disease, or complications from other medical conditions such as cancer or infections. A prosthetic hand with advanced technologies can improve the quality of life for transradial amputees. This study presents the development of a 3-D printed myoelectric prosthetic hand with a proportional control scheme and force feedback. EMG signal was used to actuate the prosthetic hand according to the user’s intention, and the grasping force applied to an object was used as a feedback signal, taken from a force-sensitive resistor (FSR) placed on the thumb’s tip. The result shows that the developed hand system has the capability to hold an object for a long time without any extra muscular effort, has an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$, and is a low-cost, less complex feedback system. Furthermore, the hand was successfully trialed on five subjects for better grasping of different objects.

articleTitle: A High-Performance CNN Hardware Accelerator for Covid-19 Feature Extraction from X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Covid-19 is a rapidly spreading disease with the potential to pose a life-threatening risk, so making prompt and accurate diagnosis of Covid-19-infected patients critically important. One method for detecting and diagnosing Covid-19 is using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to extract features from chest X-ray images. However, CNNs involve high computational complexity, requiring billions of operations per image and prolonged processing times. The aim of this paper is to design a hardware accelerator for a CNN to efficiently extract features indicative of Covid-19 from chest X-ray images. We have designed and simulated convolution unit and max-pooling unit, thereby constructing a CNN hardware accelerator for Covid-19 feature extraction from chest X-ray images. Simulation results demonstrate that the convolution unit and max-pooling unit function according to the algorithm’s specifications. Validation results also indicate the effective operation of the CNN hardware accelerator, enabling rapid and accurate detection and classification of Covid-19. With the support of the hardware accelerator, computational performance is optimized, and energy consumption is reduced, thereby enhancing the diagnostic speed of the system.

articleTitle: A Dedicated 25% Duty Cycle Clock Data Recovery for 56Gb/s PAM4 Receiver with Combined FFE+DFE
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper presents a dedicated four-phase 25% duty cycle clock data recovery (CDR) used in $56 \mathrm{~Gb} / \mathrm{s} 4$ Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM4) receiver. The CDR employs a LC quadrature voltage-controlled oscillator (LC-QVCO) and a novel bang-bang phase detector (BBPD) to achieve half rate clock firstly. Then the quarter rate clocks are generated by $\div 2$ frequency divider. Finally, the subsequent four And-gates operate them to obtain a four-phase $\mathbf{2 5 \%}$ duty cycle clock. This CDR has been designed in 65 nm CMOS process, and the total area including pads is about $0.65 \mathrm{~mm}^{2}$. Post-simulation shows that the duty cycle of four phase clock is nearly $25 \%$ under various corners and the consumed power of whole circuit is about 167 mW.

articleTitle: S-Boxes with Optimal Strict Avalanche Criterion using Chaotic Map
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Substitution boxes (S-Boxes) are essential for improving security in the modern block cipher. The main criteria to evaluate an S-Box include Nonlinearity (NL), Strict Avalanche Criterion (SAC), and Bit Independence Criterion (BIC). This paper introduces a novel approach to constructing S-Boxes with optimal SAC. The algorithm utilizes the SAC parameters of the S-Box and a newly developed chaotic map. The proposed S-Box achieved optimal values for both SAC and BIC-SAC in the cryptanalysis results, outperforming previously designed S-Boxes. Furthermore, other evaluation criteria such as Nonlinearity, Differential Approximation Probability, and Linear Approximation Probability are considered satisfactory security levels.

articleTitle: Quantum physics-based analytical model for analysing planar ohmic contacts
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Conventional analytical models for examining Metal-Semiconductor (M-S) ohmic contacts in test structures have centered around resistive-only contact interfaces. However, this approach could lead to misinterpretation, as M-S contacts are governed by the quantum physics effect of electron tunneling across the potential energy barrier at the M-S interface. This paper describes a novel resistor-to-Schottky (RSB) barrier analytical model, aiming to bridge the gap between conventional analytical approaches and the underlying physics of M-S ohmic contacts. The proposed model undergoes validation and analysis using the semiconductor device simulator tool TCAD. This study confirms the validity of the RSB model as the electrical voltage and current density profiles agree well with their counterparts extracted from the TCAD model. The investigation also highlights the differences between the proposed RSB model and the resistoronly analytical TLM expressions for contacts under different working conditions. This research contributes to a more comprehensive understanding of Metal-Semiconductor ohmic contacts, offering insights that could impact the design and interpretation of related semiconductor devices.

articleTitle: Activities for Open-Source Integrated Circuits Design in Japan
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper discusses open-source IC design. By open-source PDKs and EDA tools, IC design is experiencing big change. Conventionally, barrier to entry IC design is quite high. Open-source PDKs and EDA tools democratize IC design to all people. Many benefits are expected in research, industry, education, and so on. However, open-source IC communities are still not mature. This paper explains Japanese communities and activities for open-source IC design. In Japan, we emphasize participation of non-expert people. Some knowledge through challenging tape-out of custom analog IC is introduced.

articleTitle: Detect and Minimize Reverse Power Flow in a Distribution System Integrated Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: High penetration of renewable energy into the power system can cause risks such as overvoltage, frequency variation, voltage deviation, reverse power flow (RPF), etc. This paper presents a method to detect and minimize the reverse power flow in a distribution system integrated with renewable energy. IEEE 13 bus with a monitor is mounted on the source bus to identify the reverse power flow used to test the system. To demonstrate the induction of reverse power flow, a PV system is connected at node 692 with a set capacity of 4000 kW. The load flow is performed using co-simulation between engines OpenDSS and MATLAB through component object model server dynami-clink library. Biogeography-based optimization (BBO) is applied to solve the multiple objective functions, including RPF at the substation and total load increase at each bus. Results obtained by the proposed method show that the reverse power flow at the substation occurring due to the connection of large amounts of renewable energy sources can be significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Patient Remote Monitoring System Using MQTT Protocol for ECG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The healthcare sector is increasingly benefiting from the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT), particularly in the real-time monitoring of patients’ health conditions. One notable application involves the monitoring of electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. In this paper, we introduce an IoT-based ECG detection system utilizing the Pan-Tompkins algorithm to process ECG data, enabling early detection of cardiac irregularities and timely interventions. Our study showcases the utilization of IoT technology for remote ECG monitoring, leveraging the MQTT (Message Queuing Telemetry Transport) protocol. The system integrates components such as ESP32, AD8232 ECG Sensor, and MQTT Cloud to facilitate the real-time storage and visualization of ECG data.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of 3-DOF Delta Robot Using Dynamic Surface Control
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Currently, the optimization method for this study is to use the Dynamic Surface Control (DSC) approach for Delta robots. It assists the robot in quickly achieving the most ideal approximation motion trajectory (Tracking control) in relation to the intended trajectory, preserving system stability against unidentified external disturbances influencing joint moments, and resolving the explosion of terms problem by means of a first-order filter. The system’s stability is thoroughly established, and it is intimately related to Lyapunov stability theory. Using Matlab and Simulink tools, numerical simulation results on the figure-eight trajectory are used to assess the controller’s performance. Furthermore, the DSC controller is contrasted with Backstepping, an alternative control technique. The findings demonstrate that the DSC controller performs better than Backstepping in terms of controlling the Delta robot’s motion along the intended trajectory with less error, faster reaction times, and increased stability, particularly in situations where the system is impacted by unidentified external disturbances and when dealing with the Backstepping-related problem of term explosion.

articleTitle: A novel deep learning based method for Vietnamese ID card skew correction
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The skewness introduced during the capturing or scanning of national identity cards poses a significant challenge of accurate information extraction. In this paper, we propose a method for skew estimations and corrections specifically for Vietnamese ID cards by leveraging deep learning techniques. Firstly, YOLOv8 Instance Segmentation is employed to generate the coordinates of the contour surrounding the identification card. Subsequently, a minimum area rectangle, covering the ID card segmentation mask, is created. The skew angle is then determined by the long side of the rectangle in relation to the image’s horizontal line. Next, the ID card is rotated based on the previously calculated skew angle. In the final step, the straightened image is passed through a classification model for upside-down correction. The method was evaluated on our comprehensive, self-developed datasets, showcasing its ability to accurately detect the rotation angle for skew ID cards across a broad range of angles.

articleTitle: Flexible and Expandable RF Coil System with Soft Actuators for Deep Organ Imaging in MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This study presents a flexible and expandable RF coil system for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of deep organs, such as pituitary glands. To adjust the size of the coil, a 3D folding structure made of PDMS and soft actuators are utilized. Also, the deployable RF coil system featuring both flexibility and high conductivity is implemented using an RF coil composed of conductive polymers. A combination of stereolithography, 3D printing, and PDMS casting techniques was used to efficiently fabricate complex structures, and a system is implemented that allows coil control by soft actuators. Additionally, a remote tuning circuit was used to adjust the operating frequency of the RF coil. It is confirmed that although the operating frequency changes as the shape of the RF coil changes according to the folding structure, the operating frequency can be maintained constant by remote circuit adjustment. This technology allows for the insertion of RF coils for MRI by reducing their diameter during the process of placing them as close as possible to deep-seated organs. This presents the potential to effectively acquire MRI images of various body parts while maintaining patient comfort and improving image quality.

articleTitle: Comparison of Analog Circuit Sizing Networks and Number of Steps
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the sizing of operational amplifiers using GNNs in DLR, focusing on varying the network configurations and the number of steps per episode-a topic that has been largely untouched in previous studies. Notably, the differences in network configurations have implications for the process portability of GNNs. From our validation of four GNNs in the TSMC 180 nm process learning and the process portability of the learning model to the 65 nm process, we found that there is no significant difference between the networks at the 180 nm learning stage. However, when transitioning to the 65 nm process, the FoM of sizing by GCN exhibited a performance that is approximately 3.5 to 14 times superior to the FoM of other networks. Moreover, when comparing the performance of GCN by altering the number of steps per episode, we observed that with 15 steps or fewer, the growth rate of FoM is high in the early stages of learning but then plateaus. On the other hand, with 50 or 200 steps, the growth initially stagnates but later either surges explosively or continues to rise, ultimately achieving the highest FoM in 15,000 steps.

articleTitle: W2E (Workout to Earn): A Low Cost DApp based on ERC-20 and ERC-721 standards
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Decentralized applications (DApps) have gained prominence with the advent of blockchain technology, particularly Ethereum, providing trust, transparency, and traceability. However, challenges such as rising transaction costs and block confirmation delays hinder their widespread adoption. In this paper, we present our DApp named W2E - Workout to Earn, a mobile DApp incentivizing exercise through tokens and NFT awards. This application leverages the well-known ERC-20 and ERC-721 token standards of Ethereum. Additionally, we deploy W2E into various Ethereum-based networks, including Ethereum testnets, Layer 2 networks, and private networks, to survey gas efficiency and execution time. Our findings highlight the importance of network selection for DApp deployment, offering insights for developers and businesses seeking efficient blockchain solutions. This is because our experimental results are not only specific for W2E but also for other ERC-20 and ERC-721-based DApps.

articleTitle: Lychee Instance Segmentation at Different Growth Stages Using YOLOv8-seg Model
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to lychee instance segmentation through different development stages using the YOLOv8-seg model. A new dataset comprising 1006 lychee images from various growth phases (flowering, young fruit, green fruit, and ripe fruit) was introduced and manually labeled. We tested 5 versions of YOLOv8-seg on this dataset. The findings reveal that YOLOv8x-seg, with 71.8M parameters, achieves the highest average mAP50 accuracy of $84.1 \%$, while YOLOv8n-seg, with only 3.4M parameters, attains an mAP50 of $83.7 \%$. These results suggest that YOLOv8n-seg suits real-world applications on less powerful hardware.

articleTitle: Improving Fault Coverage of Random Pattern Test using a Scalable Distance Function
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a new method to improve the fault coverage of random test patterns generated based on a scalable distance function. The proposed patterns are made by effectively mixing pseudorandom and antirandom patterns according to a distance function. Antirandom patterns are generated by calculating hamming distance among candidates, and pseudorandom patterns are by H/W logic such as LFSR. Experimental results show the proposed method can improve the fault coverage by at least $1 \%$ up to $7 \%$ compared to the previous methods fixing the distance function. Since the proposed method can easily obtain new patterns using only the relationships between predetermined patterns, and can generate random test patterns in real time at the chip and board levels regardless of DUT size and structure, it can be widely utilized as a technology for test logic embedded in system semiconductors or semiconductor test equipment.

articleTitle: Re-structuring CNN using quantum layer executed on FPGA hardware for classifying 2-D data
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The article proposes a solution to restructure Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures by integrating parameter quantization techniques with traditional CNN models capable of deployment on Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) hardware for evaluating the classification performance of two-dimensional data in real-world scenarios. The solution introduces an additional quantum layer before the final classification layer of the CNN to receive standardized outputs, followed by computations in the Hilbert vector space to generate probability values for assessing classification results. The quantization process helps the model swiftly identify data features while optimizing the parallel computing capability of FPGA hardware. The model is evaluated on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset, revealing two advantages: time-processing on FPGA is four times faster compared to using only the Central Processing Unit (CPU) on the PynQ-z2 kit board; classification accuracy is higher when utilizing the quantum layer compared to without it, with the same number of training iterations. These results demonstrate the feasibility of hardware-accelerated AI algorithms combined with quantum algorithms in real applications.

articleTitle: RISC-V SoC with NTT-Blackbox for CRYSTALS-Kyber Post-Quantum Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The number theoretic transform (NTT) has made the computational process much faster in lattice-based postquantum cryptography algorithms, but polynomial multiplication is still the bottleneck of the process. RISC-V was introduced and demonstrated its advantages through flexibility in the instruction set architecture. This paper proposed a RISC-V SoC architecture with NTT-Blackbox that accelerates the computing capabilities of software programs running on SoCs, applied to the Kyber algorithm. The results show that the proposed architecture has improved speed from $71.5 \%$ to $\mathbf{9 9 . 3 \%}$ compared to software programs running on other RISC-V SoCs.

articleTitle: Low clock power standard cell flip-flop topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design and evaluation of several low power flip flop topologies to address the problem of large clock energy consumption for low data activity factor applications. We present a comparative analysis of clock energy, total energy, timing and the tradeoffs involved. A few promising topologies which can be used in place of conventional flops for lowering the clock energy without compromising too much on the delay and reliability are further investigated for low voltage robustness. Delay scaling with lower voltages is also examined. We show that low power flops can reduce clock energy between 20-40% at low data activity factors at an area overhead of 10-15%. Our paper also presents a complete framework to compare these flops. Standard cell versions of the flops were designed, laid out and compared post layout to obtain these results

articleTitle: Ultra-Low Power Neural Network Processors using Analog-Based Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In this paper, two types of low power and energy efficient neural network (NN) inference processors are introduced. First, an energy efficient accelerator for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) using lookup tables (LUTs) based on the vector quantization (VQ) technique is shown. VQ requires a nearest neighbor search (NNS), resulting in a large energy overhead. To overcome this issue, a timedomain associative memory (TAM) using analog-based computation is proposed. Thanks to energy efficient NNS by TAM, the proposed LUT-based CNN accelerator achieves 7.5 times higher efficiency compared with the conventional accelerators. Then, an ultra-low power NN-based audio feature extractor for keyword spotting (KWS) is demonstrated. In the conventional KWS processors, the large portion of the power of the KWS system is consumed in an analog-to-digital converter (ADC) for feature extraction. To tackle with this issue, a NN-based feature extractor is proposed in this work. It extracts audio features in analog-domain, which can remove the powerhungry ADC. Consequently, the power dissipation of the feature extraction can be reduced by $-88 \%$.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Reconfiguration Management For Smart City Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: In recent years, Blockchain technology has earned significant consideration from the smart cities developer community due to its ability to provide security, privacy, and authentication. Reconfiguration is also a challenge in IoT-based smart cities architecture, where sensor nodes need to change their behavior by the undefined conditions. In this paper, we develop a solution by integrating Blockchain into smart cities architecture to ensure security and privacy in the reconfiguring process. After deploying IoTex – an private Blockchain framework into smart cities architecture, we design a variety of smart contracts to simulate a IoT reconfiguring process. Blockchain’s features are evaluated by calculating the smart contract’s cost. On the other hand, the whole system’s performance is also measured and evaluated.

articleTitle: Advanced Timing Closure by Synopsys Tweaker™
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper presents the achievements in Timing Closure phase by using a new approach - Tweaker™ offering by Synopsys. Amongst available solutions, Tweaker® has proven to be a robust option to realize: (1) good recognition of layout rules that keeps nearly no physical error and minimum degradation from prediction and to real timing fix-rate (2) half of chip area/congestions from Hold buffers is reduced via High-Fanout Insertion (HFI) method; (3) Possible delivery shifted-left with $20 \%$ of Turn-Around-Time (TAT) reduction and up to $75 \%$ of hardware-time cost saving. From these results, we look forward to the next evolution from Synopsys Tweaker™ to PrimeClosure®.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a 2W S-band Power Amplifier for Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This article presents the design and manufacturing process of a 2 W power amplifier operating in the frequency range from 2.1 GHz to 2.5 GHz. To amplify a low power and broadband signal, the proposed power amplifier uses a 2 -stage driver amplifier and an output power amplifier, the driver amplifier uses transistor SGA-9189 with center frequencies of $\mathbf{2. 2}$ GHz and 2.4 GHz, respectively and the output power amplifier uses transistor SHF-0589 operating at a center frequency of 2.3 $\mathbf{G H z}$. The designed amplifier achieves a maximum gain of 24.5 dB in the 2.4 GHz and is greater than 23.1 dB in the 2.1 GHz 2.5 GHz band; Output power reaches 33 dBm; The input reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) reaches -13.9 dB and the output reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</inf>) reaches $\mathbf{- 1 7. 6} \mathrm{dB}$. The amplifier circuit is designed for using in wireless networks operating in the S band.

articleTitle: Designing a Compact Spiking Neural Network for Learning and Recognizing Digits on 180nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Spiking Neural Network (SNN) is one of the most promising candidates for processing immense amounts of data at high speed and low power because parallel operation is one of its key advantages. In this research, we present a complete circuit-level design, implementation, and simulation of SNN for digits classification utilizing 180nm CMOS technology, together with on-chip training and inference. The proposed SNN includes Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons and differentialamplifier-based synapses with Spike-Timing Dependent Plasticity (STDP) and Winner-Take-All mechanisms. Consequently, the proposed SNN is a compact CMOS circuit with 88 neurons and 312 synapses that is applied to the recognition of digit patterns. The average recognizing time for each digit is around $110 \mu \mathrm{s}$. Hence, the proposed SNN can recognize about 9090 patterns in one second.

articleTitle: Design neural network-based adaptive controller for underactuated 3-wheeled Mobile Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: 3-wheeled mobile robots (3WMR) are used widely in various industries. They can operate in hazardous environments and complete tasks automatically without direct human intervention. In this paper, since the 3-Wheel Mobile Robot is an insufficient actuated system, the hierarchical sliding mode controller is designed to make the 3WMR system track to the desired trajectory. Moreover, in reality, various disturbances negatively affect the system’s operation. an RBF neural network; therefore, applied to the closed scheme to estimate all the uncertainties and the system’s nonlinearities. The Lyapunov function proves the stability of the closed-loop robot system. The effectiveness of the proposed methods is verified in the simulation section by the Matlab/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: A Wideband Divide-by-2/4 Static CML Frequency Divider With Quadrature Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: A wideband divide-by-2/4 frequency divider with quadrature outputs used in phase-locked loop (PLL) is designed in 22 -nm CMOS process in this paper. The divider consists of two cascade current-mode logic (CML) dividers as high-speed pre-scaler of the PLL, a multiplexer (MUX) is employed to select the divide-by- $2 / 4$ outputs. The frequency divider core circuit dissipates 3.6 mW at 1 V supply and the division range is from 0.07 to 31 GHz when the input power is 0 dBm. The phase noise can achieve to be ${- 1 4 8. 5} \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{H z}$ or $-152 \mathrm{dBc} / \mathrm{Hz}$ at 1 MHz offset and the phase mismatch between the in-phase $(I)$ and quadrature-phase $(Q)$ is ${1. 3}$ degree or 0.8 degree for the input frequency of 12 GHz when the division ratio is 2 or 4.

articleTitle: Smart Health Monitoring Wearable with Integrated Sensors, Machine Learning, and IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The medical system comprises three primary fields: prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation. In particular, rehabilitation should always be the focus of healthcare activities, especially for the elderly. One of the global challenges facing the healthcare system is the rapid aging of the population, which creates pressure on operational costs and resources. To mitigate this pressure and provide effective healthcare services, the application of wearable device technology and the IoT offers significant potential. Therefore, a wearable device capable of monitoring oxygen saturation, heart rate based on optical sensors, as well as recognizing activities based on inertial sensors in basic daily activities (lying, sitting, standing, walking) is proposed to improve the quality of life and health of elderly individuals with reduced mobility function or during the rehabilitation process. The results showed that the developed device achieved an accuracy of $99 \%$. Furthermore, based on this wearable device, an IoT platform health monitoring and stroke alert for the elderly was developed purpose of timely warning, reducing the incidence of complications and mortality caused by stroke. This system promises to enhance and improve patient health through real-time physiological measurements. Additionally, these advancements will contribute to the creation of a comprehensive health monitoring system and promote further progress in the healthcare field.

articleTitle: A Deterministic Concurrent-Routing Algorithm to Improve Wire Selection in FPGA Routing
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: An FPGA routing architecture consists of wire segments of different lengths. FPGA routers attempt to use longer wires for distant connections and shorter ones for closer connections. Due to the overhead associated with using longer wires, FPGA routers use them only when they have delay benefits over the shorter wires. The versatile place and route (VPR) is a popular open-source FPGA placement and routing tool. This work proposes a concurrent routing-based post-routing method for VPR to improve its utilization of longer wires. The proposed method builds an archive of routing trees using the VPR’s connection router and then solves an integer linear programming (ILP) problem to select routing trees for each net in such a way that the overall wire length is reduced with no effect on the critical path delay of the circuit. Experiments using Titan 23 benchmarks showed that it could reduce the utilization of larger wires by $4.43 \%$ on average without increasing the total wire length or critical path delay.

articleTitle: Developed a Tomato-Condition Classification System using Image Processing and YOLO Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Classifying tomatoes after harvesting still heavily relies on manual labor, leading to inefficiencies and inconsistent quality. This issue affects the cost and reduces the ability to export to important international markets. This study introduces a modern solution by applying the YOLO algorithm to automate the tomato classification process. The automatic classification system is proposed, which not only reduces cost labor but also improves performance reaching approximately $98 \%$ on TOMATO dataset. This system utilizes image processing technology to assess size, color (including ripe, unripe, and rotten tomatoes), and shape (recognizing abnormalities, surface scratches,…). Additionally, the research emphasizes the importance of applying computer vision technology and utilizing self-created datasets to ensure high performance in the real-world environment of tomatoes, thus opening up prospects for technology application in agriculture.

articleTitle: Sports Activity Recognition with Deep Learning Models and Accelerometers
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Sport activity classification has become increasingly vital in various domains, including scientific research and healthcare. Accurate classification of Sports activities holds significant implications for behavior analysis and medical diagnostics. This paper investigates the classification of Sports activities using deep learning models such as Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks applied to accelerometer sensor data. The accelerometer data is collected from a wearable device affixed to the waist of individuals engaged in daily activities. The performance of the deep learning models is evaluated by training them for 100 epochs and assessing their accuracy and confusion matrices on a validation dataset. The primary aim of this research is to compare the effectiveness of different deep learning models in accurately classifying Sports activities based on accelerometer data.

articleTitle: Horizontal graph connections for skeleton-based human action recognition on UAV-Human
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are finding increasing use in surveillance, search, rescue, and many other applications. Human action recognition (HAR) using UAV data is an essential task that enables real-time detection of human behavior from visual data. The altitude and mobility of UAVs make HAR difficult. Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) architectures have achieved remarkable performance for skeleton-based HAR in recent years. While GCN is quite good at learning spatiotemporal data, it strongly relies on the dependencies of the graph definition. GCNs’ capacity to represent the relationship between large-distance joint pairs is limited. Joints at horizontal positions in the skeleton model have strong dependencies in many typical actions such as walking, running, etc. The dependencies come from the need to keep the human body balanced while moving. In this work, these dependencies are exploited by defining a graph with horizontal edges for action representation. In this way, the adjacency matrix can capture implicit dependencies of symmetric joint pairs. The performance of the GCN using horizontal graph connections is evaluated on the dataset UAV-Human. Experiments show that the proposed method outperforms SOTA methods.

articleTitle: Chaotic Multiple-image Encryption and Individual-image Decryption with FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: A large volume of image data has been increasingly generated in every area, and it is necessary to keep confidential. Multiple image encryption is a promising solution for massive image data. Existing algorithms allow to encrypt multiple images at the same time, but it is required to decrypt all cohort ciphered images to retrieve even one or a few of images. It wastes time and resource for undesired images. In this work, for the first time, a model of MIE is proposed to overcome the mentioned drawback of existing algorithms by allowing to decrypt individual images from a cohort of encrypted images. The effectiveness of the proposed model is demonstrated by the result of exemplar simulation and its FPGA implementation for the DICOM standard.

articleTitle: An Efficient Design Flow for Iterative Asynchronous Bundled-Data Circuits on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Asynchronous bundled-data circuits are promising alternatives to synchronous ones for designing low-power circuits because of their event-driven feature. However, the adoption of asynchronous circuits is hindered by limitations in commercial EDA tools, particularly concerning their ability to perform timing analysis and implement effective optimization techniques. This paper presents a design flow for implementing iterative ring-based asynchronous bundled-data circuits on FPGA with standard EDA tools. The design flow covers all essential steps, including hardware description, synthesis and implementation, and timing verification. To verify timing constraints, a novel technique called integrated timing propagation is introduced for performing timing analysis on multiple passive stages. The proposed design flow is employed to implement an advanced encryption standard circuit on the Xilinx Zynq-7000 FPGA, incorporating a phase-decoupled click template as handshaking controllers to facilitate the implementation of iterative rings. The results demonstrate that AES asynchronous BD circuits can achieve significant power savings and higher throughput-to-power ratios compared to AES synchronous circuits.

articleTitle: Dynamical Selective Image Encryption Using Chaos
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: Image data has been increasingly generated by cameras as well as acquisition modalities. Image data is diverse and has different sensitive levels. Encryption algorithms for massive image data are required not only high confidential but also high speed. Sometimes, the trade-off between the speed and confidentiality of an encryption occurs for image data, and it can be obtained with selective image encryption. However, most of existing selective image encryption algorithms are with fixed values of parameters, as a consequence, the confidentiality is threatened from cryptanalysis methods. In this paper, the scheme of selective image encryption using chaos is proposed, in which its parameters are changed dynamically. Specifically, the diffusion is carried out with dynamically selected pixels, and on its varying number of significant bits. The permutation performs on blocks of selected pixels with varying size. Intuitively, the security of the proposed scheme is improved by dynamical selective of data for the encryption. The exemplar simulation shows the effectiveness of the proposed scheme with security analysis by means of testing entropy, and correlation between neighbor pixels. The amount of data to be encrypted is also measured in compared with existing selective image encryption.

articleTitle: Enhance Security for the E-payment Application with Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: E-payment systems, despite their practicality, face challenges such as data manipulation, limited bandwidth, and potential denial-of-service attacks. These issues can impact businesses, financial institutions, and individual users conducting transactions, as they struggle to manage large amounts of traffic simultaneously. Addressing these issues is crucial for ensuring secure and efficient transactions. This research presents a system that integrates Hyperledger Fabric with software-defined networking to enhance system throughput without significantly altering the Blockchain’s functionality. It also uses Hyperledger Aries technology for improved client identity recognition efficiency. The proposed system aims to reduce deployment time, maintain secure data, and provide a non-stop payment platform for client identification within a decentralized framework. It supports multiple concurrent users or system attacks with minimal average delay, ensuring efficient communication among components. The system is being researched to find a feasible solution that balances security and performance in real time while minimizing internal platform modifications.

articleTitle: Diagnosing Electric Motor Faults based on Vibration Signals Using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: The current demand in industries is increasingly focused on early diagnosis of faults in electric motors to prevent unwanted incidents during operation. Employing machine learning to monitor and detect potential faults helps mitigate catastrophic accidents and prevent losses of both assets and human lives. A single fault occurrence can disrupt the motor’s operation, leading to malfunctions in components such as coils, bearings, etc. Detecting faults using machine learning algorithms also serves as an effective method for preventive maintenance. This study utilizes the YOLOv8 algorithm to learn characteristics from the frequency distribution of vibration signals, targeting three common types of faults in electric motors during operation. By combining feature extraction and classification, it intelligently automates fault diagnosis. The paper also provides valuable insights into the performance of the YOLOv8 network and its practical applications in the field of maintenance and industrial equipment management.

articleTitle: Design and Modelling of Machine Learning Based Photonic Sensor For Different Disease Detections
publicationTitle: 2024 9th International Conference on Integrated Circuits, Design, and Verification (ICDV)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of machine learning algorithms in conjunction with photonic sensors for the advancement of early detection technologies in healthcare. The primary objective is to establish a robust methodology utilizing light-based sensing to detect minute biological alterations, facilitating prompt diagnosis and intervention. Key aspects addressed include profiling, feature selection, model training, and validation, crucial for constructing highly accurate predictive models. The research underscores the pivotal role of this algorithm in the development of non-invasive diagnostic solutions with the potential to revolutionize healthcare delivery, enabling proactive interventions and personalized treatment strategies.
